text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which saves time for everyone on the team. One key part of clean code is following naming conventions, so variables and functions have clear, meaningful names. Another important idea is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes the code simpler to test and change. Clean code is also easier to maintain, because other developers can quickly find and fix problems. In short, writing clean code helps your whole team work faster and with fewer mistakes.
